content: 1. Buprenorphine (all forms) and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval, which can lead to serious cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 2. Calcium Acetate and Ofloxacin: Co-administration decreases the absorption of each drug in the gastrointestinal tract. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Separate administration by at least 2 hours and monitor closely. 3. Calcium Carbonate and Ofloxacin: Similar to calcium acetate, this combination reduces drug absorption in the GI tract. Separate doses by 2 hours and monitor closely. 4. Calcium Chloride and Ofloxacin: The same interaction as above applies. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 5. Calcium Citrate and Ofloxacin: Co-administration decreases drug absorption. Separate doses by 2 hours and monitor closely. 6. Calcium Gluconate and Ofloxacin: Similar interaction as other calcium salts. Separate administration by 2 hours and monitor closely. 7. Carbonyl Iron and Ofloxacin: Carbonyl iron reduces the absorption of ofloxacin in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 8. Ofloxacin and Celecoxib: There is a minor risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 9. Ceritinib and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 10. Ofloxacin and Chlordiazepoxide: Ofloxacin increases chlordiazepoxide levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but monitor closely. 11. Chloroquine and Ofloxacin: Chloroquine increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Monitor closely. 12. Chlorpromazine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 13. Ofloxacin and Cholera Vaccine: Ofloxacin may antagonize the pharmacodynamic effects of the cholera vaccine. Avoid co-administration with systemic antibiotics within 14 days of vaccination. 14. Ofloxacin and Choline Magnesium Trisalicylate: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 15. Citalopram and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, and caution is advised. 16. Clarithromycin and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 17. Clomipramine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 18. Ofloxacin and Clonazepam: Ofloxacin increases clonazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but monitor closely. 19. Ofloxacin and Clorazepate: Ofloxacin increases clorazepate levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but monitor closely. 20. Clozapine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ofloxacin and Conjugated Estrogens: Ofloxacin decreases the levels of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but additional birth control methods may be advisable. 22. Corticotropin and Ofloxacin: Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cortisone and Ofloxacin: Similar to corticotropin, this combination increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Crizotinib and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. ECG monitoring is recommended, and caution is advised. 25. Dasatinib and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Degarelix and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Desflurane and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 28. Desipramine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 29. Deutetrabenazine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. While deutetrabenazine does not significantly prolong the QT interval at recommended doses, certain conditions may increase the risk of torsades de pointes. Monitor closely. 30. Dexamethasone and Ofloxacin: Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Diclofenac and Ofloxacin: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 32. Didanosine and Ofloxacin: Didanosine reduces the absorption of ofloxacin in the GI tract. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administered, separate doses by 4–8 hours. 33. Ofloxacin and Dienogest/Estradiol Valerate: Ofloxacin decreases the levels of these hormones by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but additional birth control methods may be advisable. 34. Ofloxacin and Digoxin: Ofloxacin increases digoxin levels by altering intestinal flora, while digoxin increases ofloxacin levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Disopyramide and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 36. Dofetilide and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and dofetilide increases ofloxacin levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 37. Dolasetron and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Donepezil and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Doxepin and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 40. Dronedarone and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 41. Droperidol and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 42. Efavirenz and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Eliglustat and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Encorafenib and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 45. Entrectinib and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 46. Epinephrine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Epinephrine (Racemic) and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 48. Eribulin and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 49. Erythromycin (all forms) and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 50. Escitalopram and Ofloxacin: Escitalopram increases the toxicity of ofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Ofloxacin and Estazolam: Ofloxacin increases estazolam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but monitor closely. 52. Ofloxacin and Estradiol: Ofloxacin decreases estradiol levels by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but additional birth control methods may be advisable. 53. Ofloxacin and Estrogens (Conjugated Synthetic): Similar to estradiol, ofloxacin decreases estrogen levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Ofloxacin and Estropipate: Ofloxacin decreases estropipate levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Ofloxacin and Ethinyl Estradiol: Ofloxacin decreases ethinyl estradiol levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Ofloxacin and Ethotoin: Ofloxacin decreases the effects of ethotoin by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Ofloxacin and Etodolac: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 58. Etrasimod and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Etrasimod may also transiently decrease heart rate and delay AV conduction. 59. Ezogabine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QT interval monitoring is recommended. 60. Ofloxacin and Fenbufen: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 61. Fennel and Ofloxacin: Fennel decreases ofloxacin levels by reducing GI absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 62. Ofloxacin and Fenoprofen: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 63. Ferric Citrate and Ofloxacin: Ferric citrate decreases ofloxacin levels by drug binding in the GI tract. Administer at least 2 hours before or after ferric citrate. 64. Ferric Maltol and Ofloxacin: Ferric maltol reduces ofloxacin absorption. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 65. Ferrous Fumarate and Ofloxacin: Ferrous fumarate reduces ofloxacin absorption. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 66. Ferrous Gluconate and Ofloxacin: Ferrous gluconate reduces ofloxacin absorption. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 67. Ferrous Sulfate and Ofloxacin: Ferrous sulfate reduces ofloxacin absorption. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 68. Fexinidazole and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use alternative medications. 69. Fingolimod and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Flecainide and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 71. Fluconazole and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 72. Fludrocortisone and Ofloxacin: Co-administration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids increases the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely. 73. Fluoxetine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Fluphenazine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 75. Ofloxacin and Flurazepam: Ofloxacin increases flurazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. The clinical significance is unknown but monitor closely. 76. Ofloxacin and Flurbiprofen: There is a minor risk of CNS stimulation or seizures due to GABA receptor displacement. Monitor for adverse effects. 77. Fluvoxamine and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 78. Formoterol and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 79. Foscarnet and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Monitor closely. There is also a minor risk of tonic-clonic seizures. 80. Ofloxacin and Fosphenytoin: Ofloxacin decreases fosphenytoin effects by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Fostemsavir and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 82. Gemtuzumab and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Gepirone and Ofloxacin: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely.
